candidate: RA2 VM (ra2-games/ra2, live at ra2.games): runs the original x86 RA2 game.exe 1.006 and YR gamemd.exe 1.001 in the browser on v86, with custom firmware, a PE loader and HLE Win32/DirectX shims
lens: LEGAL & PROVENANCE: the license text, git history, Chrono Divide derivation, third-party and EA content in the repo, and whether a personal non-commercial remaster can legally build on it

refuted_claims.claim: Game files are excluded from the repo; the repo carries only the team's code, licensed dependencies and an unclear-license background (THIRD_PARTY.md, and the evaluation's framing).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: EA-owned game art is committed and deployed. public/icons/ra2.png is the RA2 Soviet-star program icon and public/icons/yr.png is the Yuri's Revenge 'Y' logo icon (I inspected both visually). public/favicon-192.png, favicon-512.png, favicon-maskable-512.png, favicon.ico and apple-touch-icon.png are upscales of the same star. All of them arrived in commit aa1eef8 ('init OSS release', author 'agent'). None is listed in docs/THIRD_PARTY.md, and they break the repo's own AGENTS.md rule against committing game content.
refuted_claims.correction: The repo is not free of EA content. A fork must delete or replace these icons, and should keep the launcher background out too, since THIRD_PARTY.md says its license is unknown and 'GPL must not be presumed'. Only then can the fork's assets be called clean.

refuted_claims.claim: Provenance report: RA2 VM has 'No Chrono Divide, ra2web or SystemJS references'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: src/ui/pages/game/styles.css has five comments that say its UI copies Chrono Divide's look: lines 577, 999, 1019, 1576 and 2136, e.g. 'referencing Chrono Divide's message-box' and 'Chrono Divide-style select ... (see its style.css)'. I compared the file against CD's style.css (scratchpad/provenance/cd/style.css, 502 rules) with a normalised selector-plus-declaration diff. None of RA2 VM's 329 rules is identical. The only shared selectors are trivial (body, 'html, body', 0%, 100%), and only one long declaration line matches (justify-content: space-between).
refuted_claims.correction: No CD code or CSS was copied, so the finding that the code is independent of CD still holds. But the web UI's look was deliberately modelled on CD's closed client. That is a low risk (visual style, no copied expression), but it is a reference, and a fork should restyle its UI rather than keep imitating CD's.

refuted_claims.claim: Provenance: 'Original work', supported by the git history.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The public history cannot show where the code came from. Commit 5758256 'init' is an empty file. Commit aa1eef8 'init OSS release' drops 454 files and 82,414 lines at once, authored by 'agent <agent@anonymous.local>'. docs/THIRD_PARTY.md cites 'PR #17, commit 9ae5cb6', but the GitHub API returns 422 for that commit and 404 for PR #17 on ra2-games/ra2, so the real history is private (AGENTS.md: 'never push dev to GitHub'). LICENSE is bare GPL text with no copyright line, and source files carry no per-file copyright headers.
refuted_claims.correction: Independence from CD rests on negative evidence: 2 of 5,343 CD literals match, 1 module path matches ('main'), and there are no CD identifiers, no 'alredy' typo and no SystemJS. My grep also found no Wine or ReactOS debug idioms (fixme:, TRACE(, WINE_, DPRINT) and no committed disassembly listings. That is strong evidence against copying from CD or Wine. It is not a verified 'original work' pedigree, and who holds the copyright is not stated, since much of the code was written by an AI agent.

refuted_claims.claim: 'It is GPL-3.0, so we can fork it legally' (score rationale), implying the base is legally usable for a personal remaster as it stands.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The GPL covers only the team's own code. The program cannot run without EA's executable, and it never takes that executable from the user. The manifest marks game.exe and gamemd.exe as 'thirdParty' and downloads them from https://oldgame.store. I checked with a HEAD request: HTTP 200, application/x-msdownload, 4,497,680 bytes, 'access-control-allow-origin: *', behind Cloudflare. That is a public redistribution of EA's binary. Every hook is locked to one SHA-256 hash, so a copy the user legally buys may be rejected if its exe bytes differ. src/games/downloadCatalog.ts and its tests link full-game downloads on uc129.com, jb51.net and archive.org. CI pulls game packages from URLs hidden in secrets (GAME_RA2_URL, GAME_RA2_YR_URL).
refuted_claims.correction: The code is legally forkable under GPL-3.0. The working product, as shipped, depends on unauthorised copies of EA binaries. A legal personal build must drop the oldgame.store fetch, downloadCatalog and CI-sourced assets, and take the exe from the user's own copy. Whether a currently sold copy (EA App or Steam) matches hashes 06f99496… and 7b8a0685… is UNVERIFIED. If it does not, the legal route means redoing every address and signature, or finding a legal way to obtain the retail 1.006 or 1.001 exe.

refuted_claims.claim: docs/THIRD_PARTY.md lists SweetFX shaders and the AMD FSR1 and ScaleFX ports with their MIT headers.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The THIRD_PARTY.md table has rows only for the dependencies, ws, LZMA-JS, Anime4K, the background image and game files. It has no rows for SweetFX, FSR or ScaleFX.
refuted_claims.correction: The notices are present elsewhere. The full MIT text sits in the headers of src/graphics/reshadePreset.ts (CeeJayDK), src/ui/pages/game/fsrUpscale.ts (AMD) and scalefxUpscale.ts (Sp00kyFox), and in src/graphics/vendor/sweetfx/LICENSE and src/ui/pages/game/vendor/README.md. This is compliant, just not indexed in THIRD_PARTY.md. It is a minor inaccuracy.

refuted_claims.claim: The IP risk is covered by 'only a non-commercial fan project is realistic', citing the HN thread that EA released source for other C&C games but not RA2.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: There is a better primary source, and the evaluation missed obligations that come with it. EA's 'Franchise Modding Guidelines' (Revision 2, 2025-02-27; copy saved at scratchpad/ea_mod.txt) list EA's GPL source releases for Tiberian Dawn, Red Alert and Renegade, with no RA2. The same guidelines give a revocable, non-commercial licence to use C&C assets in mods, on conditions. The mod must be free with no monetisation. It must display 'EA has not endorsed and does not support this product.' prominently on the website and in a root README or licence file. It must include no C&C music files, and it must not circumvent content protection. RA2 VM does not have the endorsement disclaimer: I grepped the README, docs and UI and found nothing. Separately, the EA User Agreement (https://www.ea.com/legal/user-agreement) forbids reverse engineering 'unless expressly authorized by EA or permitted by law', and the project's patches come from its own disassembly (scripts/reverse/*).
refuted_claims.correction: A fork must add EA's required non-endorsement statement, stay free with no in-game monetisation, never bundle music or other EA assets, and rely on interoperability exceptions for the reverse-engineered hooks (INFERENCE, not legal advice). EA can revoke the mod licence at any time, so the whole project exists at EA's discretion.

confirmed_claims: LICENSE is byte-for-byte identical to the official GNU GPLv3 text: I diffed it against https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt with no differences. packages/relay/LICENSE is identical too. package.json has "license": "GPL-3.0-or-later", and the README repeats it.
The GitHub API (checked 2026-09-27) shows ra2-games/ra2 was created 2026-09-12T06:51:30Z, is not a fork, has 238 stars and 33 forks, spdx GPL-3.0, last push 2026-09-21.

The first commits are 5758256 'init' and aa1eef8 'init OSS release', authored by 'agent <agent@anonymous.local>'. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md, and AGENTS.md says internal work happens on a 'dev' branch that is never pushed to GitHub.
CONTRIBUTORS.md lists Junlin Liu* (@NoCLin), Yuyuan Li (hdu.edu.cn faculty link), Lin Zhao, Jiayuan Fang and Yifan Xu.

No Chrono Divide code was found. There is no SystemJS, no ra2web identifiers, no 'alredy' typo, no paletteOffsetCount or extraLight uniforms, and no cdncache keys. The CSS shares 0 identical rules with CD's style.css; CD's influence is limited to styling comments.
src/games/yr/spawnerProbe.ts says the CnCNet yrpp-spawner GPL code was 'not copied' and that the trampoline was written independently. No YRpp, Ares or Phobos source was found in src.

The executables are auto-fetched from https://oldgame.store/game.exe and /gamemd.exe with the SHA-256 values 06f99496… and 7b8a0685… (src/games/manifest.ts, src/adapter/thirdPartyFiles.ts). The host is live and serves the file with an open CORS header.
src/games/downloadCatalog.ts links full-game downloads on uc129.com and jb51.net and an archive.org installer.
The MIT notices for SweetFX (CeeJayDK), AMD FSR1, ScaleFX (Sp00kyFox) and Anime4K (bloc97) are kept in source headers and vendor files. The LZMA-JS MIT licence is kept.

The SR model weights are not bundled: they are fetched from Hugging Face or GitHub in dev experiments. Their licence tags (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the Kim2091 models, GPL-3.0 for APISR, CC BY 4.0 for NomosUni) appear in scripts/experiments/compareSrModels.py and in the modelProbe.ts labels.
THIRD_PARTY.md itself says the launcher background has no licence and must not be presumed GPL.
No disassembly listings of EA code are committed; scripts/reverse holds only the tools.

Four of the other web RA2 repos (huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, whose old name is huangkaoya/redalert2, plus its forks OpenRA2/RA2Web and DD-Channel/ra2-web) are admitted CD derivatives. RA2 VM is not in that family, so it is the legally cleaner of the web bases with respect to CD.
verdict_notes:
From the legal and provenance angle, the central claims hold. The code really is GPL-3.0-or-later (the LICENSE matches the official text byte for byte), and I found no evidence that it comes from Chrono Divide. That makes it much cleaner than the huangkaoya family of CD-derived web ports.

The evaluation still overstates how clean it is to build on:
1. EA's icon art sits in the repo and in the deployed favicons, and THIRD_PARTY.md does not disclose it.
2. The project deliberately modelled its UI on CD's style.css. The provenance report's 'no CD references' claim is false, though no rules were copied.
3. Git history cannot establish provenance. About 82k lines landed in one anonymous 'agent' commit, the real dev history is private (THIRD_PARTY.md cites PR #17 and commit 9ae5cb6, neither of which exists publicly), and no copyright holder is named.
4. The program works only with an EA exe that it takes from a public third-party host, not from the user. It also links full-game downloads, and CI pulls game packages from hidden URLs.
5. It lacks the non-endorsement statement that EA's C&C modding guidelines require, and it relies on a 'permitted by law' interoperability reading of EA's ban on reverse engineering.

All of this can be fixed in a personal fork: remove the EA icons and the background, remove the oldgame.store fetch and downloadCatalog, take the exe from the user's own copy, add EA's disclaimer, and restyle away from CD. One uncertainty is not fixable in code. The hooks are locked to one exe hash, and it is UNVERIFIED whether a copy the user can buy legally today (EA App or Steam) has those exact bytes. If not, the legal route means redoing every hook for a new build, which weakens the 'fastest path to Step 1' argument.

I drop the score from 7 to 6. Among web bases it is still the best choice legally, provided the clean-up above happens before anything is shared, and provided the user buys the game first and checks the exe hashes before committing to the fork. Not legal advice.
